title: Migration Flows Visualisation
subtitle: Interactive Sankey and chord diagrams for intra-EU migration corridors 2010–2023
summary: Interactive Sankey diagrams for intra-EU migration 2010–2023 using D3.js.
description: Interactive Sankey and chord diagrams for intra-EU migration 2010–2023 using D3.js, sourced from Eurostat microdata. Highlights corridor concentration and net-flow asymmetries.
keyFindings: Top 5 corridors account for 38% of all intra-EU migration flows
Net-flow asymmetries between Eastern and Western EU have widened since 2015

blocks.text: Intra-EU migration data exists and is relatively high quality — Eurostat covers all 27 member states — but it is poorly communicated. The goal was to turn a dense migration matrix into something a policy audience could actually read and explore.

Data was downloaded via the Eurostat REST API (table migr_imm8) for 2010–2023, covering immigration flows between all EU27 country pairs. Python (pandas) was used to reshape the raw JSON into an origin-destination matrix for each year.

Two views were built in D3.js. The Sankey diagram shows annual net flows for the top 20 corridors. The chord diagram shows the full bilateral matrix for a selected year. Both charts animate on year change.
The top five corridors account for 38% of all intra-EU migration — a high concentration that has increased since 2015. The Romania→Germany corridor grew 210% in volume between 2010 and 2023.
